Draft a deterministic proof for the claim below using ONLY the six tools. Each tool call counts toward a 12-call budget; plan for at most lookup_source, get_premise, verify_derivation and propose_finding. Do NOT call list_dependent_claims or request_lawyer_review — they belong to other tasks and only waste your budget. Always call lookup_source for the cited source before proposing, and always call verify_derivation on the exact proof object before propose_finding — propose only a proof the checker accepted. Cite only admitted premises (lawyer_confirmed or document_extracted). Quote provision and clause text verbatim. When the checker rejects a draft, fix the flagged steps and retry. End with propose_finding carrying the full proof object.

Session matter: MAT-01. Claim id: C-REC-ASK-1017. Use the ids below EXACTLY as written — never invent, shorten or reformat an id.

Claim: Does clause 9.2 require Nimbus to keep transfer logs?
Claim type: CT2 params: {'element': 'keep transfer logs'}
As of: 2025-10-17

Target clause 9.2 Cross-border transfer for fraud screening:
Nimbus may transfer order data to its analytics cluster outside India for fraud screening. Such transfers are limited to order identifiers and risk scores, and Nimbus shall keep transfer logs for review.

Clause inventory (ref + heading):
1 Parties
2 Definitions
3 Scope of processing
4 Purpose limitation
5 Data categories
6 Security safeguards
7 Processor engagement
8 Sub-processors
9.1 Cross-border transfers, general
9.2 Cross-border transfer for fraud screening
10 Breach intimation
11 Retention and erasure

Sources (id | key | title):
SRC-DECOY | emblems-act-1950 | The Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950
SRC-DPDP-ACT | dpdp-act-2023 | The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
SRC-DPDP-RULES | dpdp-rules-2025 | The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
SRC-GSR-843E | commencement-gsr-843e-2025 | Commencement Notification G.S.R. 843(E)

Admitted premises (id | trust class | clause | statement):
F-LOOP-92 | document_extracted | CL-10 | Clause 9.2 requires Nimbus to keep transfer logs for review.
F-SEED-01 | document_extracted | CL-01 | Acme Retail Pvt Ltd is the Data Fiduciary and Nimbus Analytics Pvt Ltd is the Data Processor.
F-SEED-02 | document_extracted | CL-02 | Defines Personal Data, Processing and Breach.
F-SEED-03 | document_extracted | CL-03 | Nimbus may process Personal Data only for order fulfilment and delivery updates unless the agreement is amended in writing.
F-SEED-04 | document_extracted | CL-04 | Nimbus must not use Personal Data for advertising, profiling or incompatible purposes without Acme's prior written approval.
F-SEED-05 | document_extracted | CL-05 | Coverage is limited to customer name, contact details, delivery address and order history with no excess collection or retention.
F-SEED-06 | document_extracted | CL-06 | Nimbus must apply encryption, role-based access control and logging, reviewing measures at least once a year.
F-SEED-07 | document_extracted | CL-07 | Nimbus acts only on Acme's documented instructions and needs Acme's prior written consent to appoint a sub-processor.
F-SEED-08 | document_extracted | CL-08 | Approved sub-processors are in Schedule 1; Nimbus must notify Acme before changes and remains fully responsible for compliance.
F-SEED-09 | document_extracted | CL-09 | Nimbus must not transfer Personal Data outside India except under clause 9.2 with equivalent safeguards.
F-SEED-10 | document_extracted | CL-10 | Nimbus may transfer order identifiers and risk scores outside India for fraud screening while keeping transfer logs.
F-SEED-11 | document_extracted | CL-11 | Nimbus must intimate Acme within twenty-four hours of a Breach; Acme must then intimate the Board and affected individuals within seventy-two hours.
F-SEED-12 | document_extracted | CL-12 | Nimbus must erase Personal Data on request, withdrawal of consent, or purpose fulfilment unless law requires retention, and retain logs for minimum one year.

The proof object has exactly these fields: claim_id, as_of (YYYY-MM-DD, copy from "As of" above), conclusion ("holds" or "does not hold"), premises (list of {fact_id, statement, trust_class} copied verbatim from the admitted premises above), steps (list of step objects, the last one a conclude step). Step kinds and their fields: cite_fact {fact_id}; cite_rule {rule_card_id, citation {source_version_id, provision_id, span [start, end], sha256}} where the citation copies one provision from a lookup_source result (span [0, len(text)] of that provision, sha256 as returned); in_force {provision_id}; compare {value (number), op (one of <=, >=, ==, <, >), bound (number)}; contains_element {clause_id, quote} where quote is a verbatim substring of the target clause text above; role_applies {party, role, clause_id, quote} with the same verbatim quote rule; conclude {conclusion} repeating the proof conclusion. Prefer the smallest proof the checker accepts. The moment verify_derivation returns valid true, call propose_finding in the very next turn with the byte-identical proof object.

(1) The Central Government may notify any Data Fiduciary or class of Data Fiduciaries as Significant Data Fiduciary, on the basis of an assessment of such relevant factors as it may determine, including--- (a) the volume and sensitivity of personal data processed; (b) risk to the rights of Data Principal; (c) potential impact on the sovereignty and integrity of India; (d) risk to electoral democracy; (e) security of the State; and (f) public order.

(2) The Significant Data Fiduciary shall--- (a) appoint a Data Protection Officer who shall--- (i) represent the Significant Data Fiduciary under the provisions of this Act; (ii) be based in India; (iii) be an individual responsible to the Board of Directors or similar governing body of the Significant Data Fiduciary; and (iv) be the point of contact for the grievance redressal mechanism under the provisions of this Act; (b) appoint an independent data auditor to carry out data audit, who shall evaluate the compliance of the Significant Data Fiduciary in accordance with the provisions of this Act; and (c) undertake the following other measures, namely:--- (i) periodic Data Protection Impact Assessment, which shall be a process comprising a description of the rights of Data Principals and the purpose of processing of their personal data, assessment and management of the risk to the rights of the Data Principals, and such other matters regarding such process as may be prescribed; (ii) periodic audit; and (iii) such other measures, consistent with the provisions of this Act, as may be prescribed.
", "sha256": "031853e2825646c3b668897e71079fd8a85295287e75b38a570ee29a713c9707"}, {"provision_id": "PRV-DPDP-Act-2023-s11-V2SIM", "key": "DPDP-Act-2023_s11", "text": "11. Right to access information about personal data.

(1) The Data Principal shall have the right to obtain from the Data Fiduciary to whom she has previously given consent, including consent as referred to in clause (a) of section 7 (hereinafter referred to as the said Data Fiduciary), for processing of personal data, upon making to it a request in such manner as may be prescribed,--- (a) a summary of personal data which is being processed by such Data Fiduciary and the processing activities undertaken by that Data Fiduciary with respect to such personal data; (b) the identities of all other Data Fiduciaries and Data Processors with whom the personal data has been shared by such Data Fiduciary, along with a description of the personal data so shared; and (c) any other information related to the personal data of such Data Principal and its processing, as may be prescribed.

(2) Nothing contained in clause (b) or clause (c) of sub-section

(1) shall apply in respect of the sharing of any personal data by the said Data Fiduciary with any other Data Fiduciary authorised by law to obtain such personal data, where such sharing is pursuant to a request made in writing by such other Data Fiduciary for the purpose of prevention or detection or investigation of offences or cyber incidents, or for prosecution or punishment of offences.
", "sha256": "23ad0c27f369650e94132bb706fbb743c09e1b72a58ea59eaa526cb190d73d40"}, {"provision_id": "PRV-DPDP-Act-2023-s12-V2SIM", "key": "DPDP-Act-2023_s12", "text": "12. Right to correction and erasure of personal data.

(1) A Data Principal shall have the right to correction, completion, updating and erasure of her personal data for the processing of which she has previously given consent, including consent as referred to in clause (a) of section 7, in accordance with any requirement or procedure under any law for the time being in force.

(2) A Data Fiduciary shall, upon receiving a request for correction, completion or updating from a Data Principal,--- (a) correct the inaccurate or misleading personal data; (b) complete the incomplete personal data; and (c) update the personal data.

(3) A Data Principal shall make a request in such manner as may be prescribed to the Data Fiduciary for erasure of her personal data, and upon receipt of such a request, the Data Fiduciary shall erase her personal data unless retention of the same is necessary for the specified purpose or for compliance with any law for the time being in force.
", "sha256": "8a75b688e24f12c2fa0dd3110f7c1b2efda61dc3b3d7d7c276e9d4f87e3c14d5"}, {"provision_id": "PRV-DPDP-Act-2023-s13-V2SIM", "key": "DPDP-Act-2023_s13", "text": "13. Right of grievance redressal.

(1) A Data Principal shall have the right to have readily available means of grievance redressal provided by a Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager in respect of any act or omission of such Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager regarding the performance of its obligations in relation to the personal data of such Data Principal or the exercise of her rights under the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.

(2) The Data Fiduciary or Consent Manager shall respond to any grievances referred to in sub-section

(1) within such period as may be prescribed from the date of its receipt for all or any class of Data Fiduciaries.

(3) The Data Principal shall exhaust the opportunity of redressing her grievance under this section before approaching the Board.
